messages:
sam (oncall): seeing a short surge of 502/504s from us-east -> eu-west at 08:23 UTC, looks correlated with LB retries and a bunch of DNS SERVFAILs. anyone else seeing this?
alex (eng-net): I pulled edge-dns logs — around 08:22 we hit a per-region DNS rate limiter for eu-west resolvers, queries dropped to 0 for ~18s. lots of retry attempts stacked at the LB layer.
maria (sre): that matches tracing — requests retried 2-3x before hitting fallback. user impact ~3.2% for traffic to that region for those 30s.
jenny (netops): we rolled a DNS resolver config change at 07:50 to add stricter per-client qps limits (recent security tweak). rollback?
alex (eng-net): yep, the new limiter buckets were conservative. they interact poorly with our LB healthcheck/jitter pattern — many healthchecks looked like abusive clients.
sam (oncall): deploy-bot shows the change: deploy-bot: deployment 2026-11-13T07:50Z "dns-rate-limiter-v2" -> eu-west.
maria (sre): immediate mitigation: can we enlarge the token bucket for lb-healthchecks in eu-west and increase burst window?
jenny (netops): I can bump threshold to previous values and add a short cooldown to healthcheck spike detection. willing to do emergency rollback if needed.
alex (eng-net): also TTLs are too low on a few service records (10s). when the limit kicked in, caches expired and clients refetched which amplified qps. suggest raising to 60s for lb records.
sam (oncall): action list then: 1) jenny to increase limiter threshold in eu-west to pre-rollout within 15m (owner: jenny) 2) alex to audit LB healthcheck qps pattern and add jitter tuning by EOD (owner: alex) 3) maria to create a short alert for DNS SERVFAIL spike tied to retries (owner: maria) 4) alex/jenny to raise TTLs for lb service records to 60s and document rationale in runbook (owner: alex, jenny) 5) ops to add a canary gate for future dns-rate-limiter rollouts (owner: netops team)
alex (eng-net): I'll also add an automated test that simulates healthcheck bursts under limiter to staging. target: PR by end of day.
maria (sre): timeline note: follow-ups / retro next week — want to check recurring pattern: we've seen small DNS-limiter interactions twice in last 6 weeks (cf. incident 1799004444 and 1845032100) — we should consider a cross-region review.
sam (oncall): assigning owners in thread: jenny -> emergency threshold bump (15m), alex -> LB healthcheck tuning + TTLs (EOD), maria -> alert + retro ticket (COB), ops -> rollout gating (next sprint).
jenny (netops): bumped limiter thresholds at 08:35 UTC, monitoring now. no more SERVFAILs in the last 10m.
maria (sre): confirmed user errors dropped back to baseline after bump. logging saved for postmortem.
alex (eng-net): opening a follow-up ticket with checklist: pre-rollout sim -> runbook update -> staging canary -> production gate. will link PRs.
sam (oncall): good work. pls add owners and ETA to the postmortem follow-up doc. I'll close incident channel when tickets are created. :thumbsup:
maria (sre): created retro ticket INF-4721 and assigned owners + tentative retro date. linking logs and alert graphs in the ticket.
deploy-bot: rollback not required — emergency config patch applied by netops at 08:35 UTC.
jenny (netops): will schedule a dedicated cross-region DNS limiter review for next week.
sam (oncall): last check: 09:05 UTC traffic stable, marking incident as mitigated. we'll reconvene for the retro. thanks everyone. :coffee:
